steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Urbanisation: % urban pop increasing; megacities >10M; counterurbanisation (rich to rural); reurbanisation (gentrification)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: DTM: Stage 1 (high BR/DR), 2 (falling DR), 3 (falling BR), 4 (low BR/DR), 5 (BR<DR); Pyramids: expanding, stationary, contracting

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Migration: push (war, poverty, enviro) vs pull (jobs, safety, services); Lee's model

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Development: HDI (health, education, income); GNI per capita; inequality (Gini, Lorenz)

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Explain how a country's position in the Demographic Transition Model affects its population pyramid shape --- Solution: Stage 2 (e.g. Nigeria): high BR, falling DR -> wide base (many young), narrow top (few elderly), pyramidal. Stage 4 (e.g. UK): low BR, low DR -> narrower base, wider top, columnar. Stage 5 (e.g. Japan): BR<DR -> contracting base, bulge at top, inverted pyramid

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Compare urbanisation in LIC vs HIC | Interpret a population pyramid for Stage 3 | Explain push/pull factors for rural-urban migration

steps.title: Lesson plan
steps.body: Starter (5 min): Recall prior knowledge of human geography with quick questions. Teaching (15 min): Work through each of the learning objectives, explaining principles step by step. Key points review (5 min): Revisit the key points together, confirming understanding.
